Newer versions of Sketch open old files just fine, and licenses are valid for any version. Sketch licenses do not 'expire', you simply can't receive updates any longer, so you can keep working on your version indefinitely without being locked out.
I can't open any of our old sketch files at work because I don't have a valid license for a version that works on the newest OS.
Sketch performance feels like a web app. Figma feels native. On every platform. Go figure.

Sketch is great software, well built, but the fact that in late 2020 they still have to write 'And soon, the ability to collaborate in real-time' is the best counter-argument to building native for me personally.
It's not just their commitment to Desktop, but their commitment specifically to not move off MacOS where they have stated that they 'will not consider supporting Sketch' on Windows/Linux.
A browser-based version of Sketch would be huge - this is Figma's killer USP at the moment.
My issue with Figma is that it feels slow and clunky to me, I imagine largely because it has to run in a browser. Surprised so many people prefer it [over Sketch].
Figma canvas is silky smooth while Sketch drones on.
Figma is rather performant (to the point where it outruns Sketch in typical day-to-day design tasks), and their vector-editing is less buggy [than Sketch's].
You don't have to pay to keep using Sketch, as long as you're ok with not upgrading. Unlike Adobe creative cloud that stops functioning the moment you don't pay.
Sketch runs on about every mac you can buy, you don't really need a big expensive computer to use it, unlike Photoshop or Illustrator.

Sketch is great as a design system manager. It's not all that great as a sketching tool (in spite of the name) and is a terrible photo editor. It shines when you embrace Sketch symbols and libraries, allowing DRY, component-based designs.

It's light, fast, cheap, easy to use and has excellent support for reusable components, making working with design systems a breeze. Adobe have been working on XD for years and are still nowhere close.
The file format is basically zipped json files, so there's a robust plugin ecosystem and you can do things like git integration pretty easily. And it's a native Mac app, unlike Figma.

Sketch has been widely adopted for UI design. It's simpler than Adobe Illustrator, lighter in resources and subjectively feels far less clunky in use. Additionally, Sketch has a massive collection of plugins that forms a large part of its appeal.

We have just recently started using React for new products, doing the design in Sketch. This was already a huge improvement in efficiency compared to doing design in Photoshop and building products with Angular.

Sketch is incredible. I wish there was something like it available on Linux, or I could run it on Linux somehow. Seeing how important a tool it's becoming to web design makes me uneasy as it's shutting out my ability to do anything design related.
